headline: Data Centers Pay Own Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, primarily data centers, to bear the costs of dedicated grid infrastructure, aiming to reduce the burden on residential ratepayers.
supporters: Governor Abigail Spanberger, State Corporation Commission (SCC), consumer advocacy groups, residential ratepayers, Dominion Energy, Piedmont Environmental Council.
opponents: Data centers, large industrial users, Data Center Coalition.
news_headline: Virginia cracks down on electricity firms hiking prices for AI data centers
news_summary: Virginia is now requiring data centers to cover electricity infrastructure costs driven by their growing power demands, a move state officials believe could save ordinary electricity customers hundreds of millions of dollars. The State Corporation Commission ordered data centers to pay for transmission infrastructure used exclusively by their facilities, preventing utilities from spreading these costs across their wider customer base.

headline: Report Data Center Water Use
short_summary: This bill mandates waterworks operators to categorize and report water usage by data centers, enhancing transparency and aiding state water supply planning.
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities concerned about water resources, State Sen. Kannan Srinivasan, Virginia Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ).
opponents: Data centers (potential due to reporting burden).
news_headline: New regulations beef up data centers' required water use reporting in Virginia
news_summary: New regulations, effective next January, will increase transparency on data center water usage in Virginia by requiring waterworks operators to categorize monthly sales data, including usage by data centers. This legislation, carried by State Sen. Kannan Srinivasan, aims to fill data gaps and provide the Department of Environmental Quality with better information for water supply planning, especially during droughts.

headline: Regulate Data Center Location and Noise
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby homes and schools, and allowing localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental and conservation groups, Virginia League of Conservation Voters, Governor Spanberger.
news_headline: Sterling Resident Says Data Center's Generators Produced Excessive Noise, Pollution
news_summary: A Sterling resident reported excessive noise and fumes from a data center's backup generators, forcing him to leave his home and highlighting a lack of regulatory authority to address such incidents. This incident underscores community concerns about data center noise pollution, prompting local officials to consider initiatives for regulating backup generators and stricter noise ordinances.
